(opens in a new tab) How prepaid and postpaid billing work, when you're charged, and how to switch to postpaid. On this page Overview Check your billing type Prepaid and postpaid compared When you’re charged Overdue invoices Switch from prepaid to postpaid Where to go next Every account is either prepaid (you pay first, then use the service) or postpaid (you use the service, then pay a monthly invoice). New accounts are prepaid. On a free trial? Free trial accounts are always prepaid. Postpaid billing is only available once your account is active, and direct debit is only available for postpaid accounts. See Your free trial . Check your billing type Section titled “Check your billing type” Go to Billing › Home . Your billing type is shown under Type , next to your account name and number. The Balance box shows your current balance, your Credit limit and your Billing date . Prepaid and postpaid compared Section titled “Prepaid and postpaid compared” Prepaid Postpaid How you pay Top up your balance in advance. Subscriptions and calls are taken from it. Pay an invoice each month for the previous month’s subscriptions and usage. Invoices A tax invoice and receipt are created and emailed with every top-up. No monthly invoice. An invoice is issued on the 1st of each month, with 14-day payment terms. Credit limit How far your balance is allowed to go below zero. Shown in the Balance box. It’s $0 unless the support team has given you one. Set by the accounts team, based on your security deposit. Your balance can go below zero as far as the credit limit. What happens if you go over Outgoing calls and outgoing SMS stop when your balance drops to $0, or to your credit limit if the support team has given you one (for example, −$10 with a $10 credit limit). New calls stay blocked until you top up. Calls stop once your balance drops to the credit limit. Deposit None. A fully refundable security deposit equal to one month’s subscriptions and usage. Best with Automatic top-ups and low balance notifications . Automatic payments for each invoice. A call that’s already in progress when the balance runs out isn’t cut off: it finishes normally, and only new calls are blocked. Monthly fees are still charged to your balance while outgoing calls and SMS are stopped. For example, a postpaid account with a $100.00 credit limit keeps working until its balance reaches −$100.00. To raise your credit limit, contact the support team. When you’re charged Section titled “When you’re charged” These apply to every account, prepaid or postpaid: Subscriptions (licences, numbers and plans) are charged on the 1st of each month. Included call value on call plans resets on the 1st of each month. Check the critical information summary for your plan to see what’s included. New services are charged pro rata. When you order a service partway through the month, you pay only for the days left until the end of the month. Included call value is reduced in the same way, except on unlimited plans, which give unlimited calls straight away. From the next 1st, you pay the full monthly amount. For example, if a service costs $20.00 a month and you order it with half the month left, you’re charged $10.00 for that month. Your monthly subscription total is listed under Active subscriptions in Account details . Overdue invoices Section titled “Overdue invoices” If an invoice becomes Overdue and stays unpaid, a penalty is deducted from your balance after 10 days, and your account is suspended after 30 days. See Invoices . Switch from prepaid to postpaid Section titled “Switch from prepaid to postpaid” Raise a support ticket to ask for postpaid billing. Include your account number. The accounts team contacts you to arrange the security deposit. Once the deposit is paid, they move your account to postpaid and set your credit limit. If the request doesn’t come from an authorised contact on the account, it can’t be processed.
